engine: Official native Godot 4.7.2, Arch Linux / Wayland, NVIDIA RTX 3070 Laptop
launch_behavior: Start screen. Begin then Ready. No automatic shutdown.

encounter.end: British roadside patrol and subtitled tea scene

systems: Sight-confirmed shooting, uncertain sound investigation, squad contact reports
Alternating assault movement, cover selection, defensive digging and near-miss suppression
Finite shared combat/loot inventory, reloads, knives and weapon breakage
Breda M37: 20 loaded rounds plus three 20-round reserve feed trays, gunner falls back to rifle
Local mesh/collision destruction, ground excavation, material resistance, dynamic ground navigation
Optional one-at-a-time wired demolition satchel: place, lob, recover, detonate, finite cable
Openable and breakable doors, mantling, roof ramps
Shared tactical controller for friendly actors; patrol appears after the combat

controls_added.F: Doors, loot, MG mount/dismount, recover charge

historical_notes: Carcano uses six-round en-bloc clips, not five-round stripper clips
Breda M37 uses 20-round rigid trays and different ammunition from the Carcano
Fictional village near Capuzzo, 14 June 1940; period-informed stone/plaster architecture
Demolition prop is period-style; exact June 1940 Italian issued kit not established. Carry and cable limits are game rules.
limitations: Original simplified prototype art and animations; not AAA production quality
Local geometric destruction is not general structural collapse or a structural-engineering simulation
Finite encounter boundary and 24-metre solid ground depth
No automatic timer on demolition satchels; they use the game cable and detonator
Tactical balance and feel still need human testing
Friendly combat controller is verified but the normal British patrol arrives after hostiles are cleared
No multiplayer, campaign save, voice acting or controller mapping
